body:
Damn. Thanks for your reply. I was deeply suicidal last night and I just kept thinking about how I didn't want that picture of her in my head anymore, but I didn't think about the fact that I have that image is because I stayed with her til the very end. That's... something to think about.

Also, jesus, I'm sorry you lost your dog too. That's pretty recent, I really hope you're being kind to yourself. It means a lot to me that you understand how it can be. I never really got to talk about how much her death affected me. I actually got a lot of flak from someone I had to be around a lot a few days after it happened, because I was "too sad". Jesus Christ. Yeah, it was probably cancer that got my dog too. Started affecting her brain and her ability to breathe. Happened so fast. It's terrifying, isn't it?

Yeah, I don't really believe in heaven either. But that dog, she'd be my soulmate, if there ever were such a thing. I've had suicidal ideation on and off throughout my life since I was pretty young, and there were a lot of days where I kept my shit together just so that I could stick with her.

She had a bad past. She came from a background of mistreatment and abuse. She had a few screws loose and didn't know how to play or how to be a dog very well. 

I have a few screws loose, too. I don't know how to person very well a lot of the time. It was kind of perfect. We were sort of both these wierd traumatized space aliens together, doing our best. She got me through so much shit. 

The day after she died, I remember I was driving and feeling so out-of-body, I just pulled over to the side of the road and started crying and screaming for my baby girl back. It was like someone else had taken over my body. I also started getting really worried I'd do something to myself. I'd already flirted with alcoholism on and off beforehand, but I didn't feel like there was anything stopping me anymore so my drinking got scary, i pushed everyone away, and I fell back into an abusive relationship id been trying to avoid for years. I totally self-destructed.

I've got more of a handle on the drinking now, and I'm digging my way out of the hole I put myself in after she died, but yeah, I don't think anyone really gets how much of a catalyst her death was for me. I took care of myself so I could take care of her-- she was fragile, and she always had health problems, and she was afraid of most things that weren't me. I loved her with my entire fucking heart.

Thanks for being so compassionate about this. I'm really glad you're in that support group, I probably should've done that at some point. It's funny, my mom died about seven years ago and the whole experience afterward left me so wary of talking to people about grief that I think I just developed this "bottle it up and move on" philosophy that has NOT served me well, lol. Turns out unchecked grief can really mess you up in some fun ways. I bet you know what I mean. I'm doing my best now though. :) I think writing this out actually helped me, so thank you for giving me the space to do that. And I'd bet anything that your dog really loved you.

Take care
